setup.deploy/k8s/api.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: courier-api
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: courier-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: courier-api
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: courier-api
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: registry.courier.example/api:2.4.1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
            - containerPort: 9090
          env:
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: postgresql://courier:Courier-Prod-2026!@courier-db:5432/courier
            - name: SESSION_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: courier-api
                  key: session-key
setup.deploy/k8s/access.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: courier-api
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: courier-api
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: courier-api
    namespace: default
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
setup.deploy/k8s/services.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: courier-api
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: courier-api
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: courier-api-metrics
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: courier-api
  ports:
    - name: metrics
      port: 9090
      targetPort: 9090
setup.deploy/k8s/db.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: courier-db
spec:
  serviceName: courier-db
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: courier-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: courier-db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:17.4
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
      volumes:
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {}
setup.docker-compose.yml:
# Local development.
services:
  api:
    build: services/api
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://courier@courier-db.production.courier.example:5432/courier

defects.title: The production database password is written in the API's deployment file
The API's service account is bound to cluster-admin, so it can do anything in the cluster
The API's metrics port has its own public load balancer
The database keeps its data in a temporary volume with no backups, so a restart loses everything
Local development connects to the production database
Nothing but people applying the manifests by hand puts a change into the cluster: there's no pipeline
